name: Ouroboros Energy Atmospheric Carbon Capture Network
product_name: Ouroboros Energy Atmospheric Carbon Capture Network
description: A network of industrial facilities that extract carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and convert it into useful materials — carbon fiber, graphene, diamond, and hydrocarbon fuels. The ACCN uses chemical sorbents to capture CO2 from ambient air and catalytic processes to transform it into solid carbon products. The system is energy-intensive but powered by Ouroboros's micro-fusion reactors, making it effectively carbon-negative. The captured carbon is used in manufacturing, creating a closed loop where atmospheric pollution becomes industrial feedstock.
base_technologies: Carbon material fabrication from atmospheric feedstock
enables: Graphene and carbon fiber from atmospheric sources
social_impact: The ACCN has made carbon a harvested resource rather than a waste product, and Ouroboros sells the captured carbon materials at prices that undercut conventional carbon manufacturing. The system has also given Ouroboros a claim to environmental virtue that deflects criticism of their other operations — they are literally cleaning the air while simultaneously controlling the energy supply. Environmental activists note that the ACCN treats the symptom of atmospheric pollution while Ouroboros's energy monopoly enables the industrial activity causing it.
story_hooks: An ACCN facility has been capturing something other than carbon from the atmosphere — the chemical sorbents have concentrated a previously undetected atmospheric compound that someone was dispersing at levels too low for standard detection.

Ouroboros is using ACCN carbon capture as leverage in climate negotiations — threatening to reduce atmospheric cleanup if regulatory conditions are not met, essentially holding the atmosphere hostage.
